<details>
<summary>AI feedback</summary>

Reviewed at 35512c0. Lint and the build pass.

**Blockers**

- web-platform-tests/wpt#64800 needs a test with two `document.write()` calls inside a text-mode element. Chromium doesn't [flush at the end of the document write steps](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/35512c05b2f30f334169e3a5b77514603641425b/source#L126268-L126273) there.
  - In the Blink source, [`kDeferTreeBuilderFlush`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/dc5f94700f3bf024c0ed3827719fd729e9b029c7/third_party/blink/common/features.cc#L428) is enabled by default.
  - In the "text" insertion mode, [`HTMLTreeBuilder::Flush()`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/dc5f94700f3bf024c0ed3827719fd729e9b029c7/third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/parser/html_tree_builder.cc#L3253-L3296) flushes immediately only the first time per element. After that it throttles: 16 ms at first, doubling up to 2 s.
  - So `doc.write("<textarea id=t>a"); doc.write("b"); t.value` would give "a" in Chromium, where this PR requires "ab". The same goes for `<title>` and `document.title`.
  - The existing textarea test writes only once before checking, so it doesn't catch this. Chromium would fail the new test, so it needs a bug.

- web-platform-tests/wpt#64800 also needs tests for a stray DOCTYPE, a comment appended to the Document, and a whitespace run after `</body>`. Gecko doesn't [flush on every non-character token](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/35512c05b2f30f334169e3a5b77514603641425b/source#L146815-L146817). In the Gecko source:
  - [`nsHtml5TreeBuilder::doctype()`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/935e9f7e39fcb9d738d3ac064905dcf4cc0c9cfc/parser/html/nsHtml5TreeBuilder.cpp#L214-L239) never calls `flushCharacters()`.
  - [`comment()`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/935e9f7e39fcb9d738d3ac064905dcf4cc0c9cfc/parser/html/nsHtml5TreeBuilder.cpp#L241-L265) skips the flush for comments appended to the Document (initial, before html, after after body, and after after frameset modes).
  - [`characters()`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/935e9f7e39fcb9d738d3ac064905dcf4cc0c9cfc/parser/html/nsHtml5TreeBuilder.cpp#L347-L357) flushes before each whitespace character in the after body, after after body, and after after frameset modes.

  So in Gecko:
  - `a<!DOCTYPE html>b` in body gives no characterData record, versus one per this PR.
  - `</html> <!--x--> ` records the comment before the text.
  - `x</body>  ` gives two characterData records instead of one.

  Blink and WebKit match this PR in all three cases, so the PR's rule is right and Gecko needs a bug.

**Nits**

- [*flush pending text*](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/35512c05b2f30f334169e3a5b77514603641425b/source#L147530-L147531) could use the modern intro, "To <dfn>flush pending text</dfn>:", like *insert a foreign element*. It currently says "When the steps in this specification require the user agent to flush pending text, the user agent must run the following steps:".
- [The *replace data* call](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/35512c05b2f30f334169e3a5b77514603641425b/source#L147549-L147551) could label its arguments the way DOM's `appendData()` does: "replace data with node *previousSibling*, offset *previousSibling*'s data's length, count 0, and data *data*".

</details>

> AI feedback

Done. Added test cases, and opened gecko/chromium bugs based on this review (see OP).

<details>
<summary>AI feedback</summary>

Reviewed at 5f89cb7. Lint and the build pass, and the earlier blockers and nits are addressed. In the main parser test of web-platform-tests/wpt#64800, CI shows Chrome failing only the three text-mode `document.write()` tests and Firefox failing only the six Gecko tests. A local WebKit build passes all nine.

**Blockers**

- WebKit needs a bug too. In a local WebKit build, the [first subtest](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/8ca3f5ca893aef8400bcc8f539a6cb18354ba185/html/syntax/parsing/parser-text-node-coalescing-and-mutations.html#L22-L50) fails: it gets one characterData record where this PR requires none.
  - In the data state, WebKit's tokenizer [ends the current character token at any `<`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/243fc8a13060335a74b08f734bdc8ac4d6188b70/Source/WebCore/html/parser/HTMLTokenizer.cpp#L281-L285), even when no tag follows. So `b<1c` is inserted as `b` and then appended to.
  - Character references and NUL don't split runs, and neither does text in RCDATA, RAWTEXT, script data, or PLAINTEXT.
  - Chrome and Firefox pass this subtest.

  The PR description says "WebKit: already matches for document parsing", so please file a WebKit bug and list it there.

</details>
